This baseline run is obtained by concept-based information retrieval system. The query-document similarity consists of phrase-similarity and term similarity.

The run is obtained by a concept-based information retrieval system. Each document's similarity consists of a phrase similarity and a term similarity. Each query is tried to retrieved a synonym in wikipedia. Moreover, we utilize three methods of query expansions, web feed back, wikipedia feed back and pseudo feed back. For each query, it is retrieved on the basis of concept in the query, query terms and 20 epansion terms.

We used Indri to index the permalinks files. The query was formulated such that the presence of title words is enforced in the retrieved documents. We used pseudo relevance feedback to boost the performance.

We used Indri to index the permalinks files. The query was formulated using a weighted combination of a) title words, b) noun phrases in the description, and c) words in description. We used pseudo relevance feedback to boost the performance.

This is our most basic run, which simply re-ranks each term according to how many sentiment terms exist in each document, normalized over the size of the document being examined. Serves almost like a baseline run for the opinion retrieval portion.

This method incorporates our method B strategy which re-ranks documents only by sentiment weights, except incorporating the tf-idf formula for each document. The tf-idf formula is isolated to *sentiment* terms found in the document only. No target terms are considered in this run, as future runs (other methods) will incorporate target terms as well.

We used several techniques for mining the data. The CDIP collection was processed using Perl and other Unix scripts to cleanse the content. We then used Clearwell E-Discovery Platform and other third-party eDiscovery packages to extract documents based on keywords, boolean search, fuzzy search and concept search. We then used iterative searching techniques driven by human review. Quality control was based on a sample (95% confidence level) with review of both the non-responsive collection and responsive collection, followed by native export. The final stage was to consolidate and clean the submission using another set of Unix scripts and Perl scripts.

We used the online search system of UCSF Legacy Tobacco Documents Library. Our main effort was on query formulation. We tried many queries, read many retrieved documents, and had quite a few clarification emails with the topic authority. Our submitted results contain documents retrieved using four separate Boolean queries. Each of the four queries aims at certain groups of responsive documents, and we feel together they give better search results in  terms of both recall and precision. No degree of relevance is implied in the order of the submitted documents because the system is a pure Boolean system.

The documents from each unique host name were grouped and indexed as separate collections.  Each host collection was represented as a "big document" in a vector space of approximately 400,000 terms.  Each topic was projected into the term vector space.  The host collections were ranked relative to each topic-vector using vector space model cosines with the host-by-term matrix.  The topic was run against the top 50 ranked hosts with Lucene and the ranked results from each host were merged using a standard result set merge algorithm.
